labeling_method: Read the article text EXACTLY as the model receives it: the first 8000 characters of dev raw_articles.body_text, which is the truncation at src/enrichment/snippet_extractor.py:40. The tail of a long article is deliberately NOT labeled, because the model never sees it.

For each article, pick the snippets a careful human editor would keep under the four criteria the production prompt itself states (snippet_extractor.py:44-48): direct quotes from NAMED sources, key statistics with context, important factual claims, definitive statements about events. At most 5, matching max_snippets=5.

Label every field the prompt asks for: type (one of the 5 the prompt enumerates, never a new value), entities (names that the snippet is actually about), confidence (0-100, how sure a human is that this belongs in the article), position (0-1 fraction into the 8000-char window, estimated from the character offset).
Labels were written WITHOUT looking at any pipeline output, so they do not encode the pipeline's current behaviour. The article text is the only input.

Reproduction: for a given article_id, the label is a deterministic function of the text. A second labeller needs only eval/data/corpus.json, the dev row, the four criteria quoted above, the five type values from the prompt, and the field definitions in eval/README.md. Agreement is measurable per field because the harness scores one field at a time.
known_limitations: Inter-annotator agreement is NOT measured: there is only one labeller (me). Every number here should be read as a single-annotator baseline, not a ceiling. The first honest follow-up is a second labeller over 10 of these 30 and a per-field kappa.

The gold is a judgement about 'the snippets a human would keep'. A defensible alternative labeller would choose different sentences. Snippet_found recall is therefore bounded above by annotator agreement, not by 1.0.

For non-English articles, entities are labeled in the source language (as the prompt's 'exact snippet text' requires). If the model answers in English, snippet_found collapses to 0 -- which is a real finding about the field, not a matching artifact, and the harness reports a script_overlap diagnostic so the two can be told apart.

b487581e-fc63-4ba1-ab75-7f570e3c986c.title: Amnesty urges Iran to halt flogging of female singer Parastoo Ahmadi
b487581e-fc63-4ba1-ab75-7f570e3c986c.labeler_notes: 21166-char rolling-news digest on reddit.com covering three unrelated stories (Amnesty/Iran, Trump on the war, Houthi resupply) plus a fourth on the Basij. Headline is only the first story. This is the hardest gold in the set: a correct extractor should concentrate on the story the headline names, and the harness will show whether it does.

snippets.text: Amnesty International on Thursday called on Iranian authorities to immediately halt plans to flog singer Parastoo Ahmadi and eight others over a livestreamed 2024 concert in which she performed without a hijab and sang in public despite Iran’s ban on solo performances by women.
snippets.note: The headline story, stated completely: who Amnesty called on, over what, and why.

snippets.text: The rights group said Ahmadi and the others were each sentenced in June to 74 lashes, a two-year travel ban and a two-year ban on artistic activities. An appeals court in Qom upheld the convictions and sentences on Sept. 25, making the rulings final and enforceable.
snippets.note: 74 lashes, two-year travel ban, two-year artistic ban, upheld on a specific date. The hard numbers of the lead story.

snippets.text: Amnesty described flogging as “cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment” that violates the absolute prohibition on torture and other ill-treatment.
snippets.note: Amnesty's own quoted characterization of the punishment.

snippets.text: "I've destroyed their nuclear capability. I've destroyed their navy, 159 ships are at the bottom of the sea. I've destroyed their air force. All their planes are gone. I've destroyed their radar," he said.
snippets.note: The most quotable Trump line in the digest, with 159 ships, a concrete number inside the quote.

snippets.text: He said Iranian authorities had killed between 72,000 and 75,000 protesters in protests earlier this year.
snippets.note: 72,000 to 75,000 protesters killed; the most consequential unverified figure in the article and therefore the one a careful editor must surface rather than bury.
